transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-02
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Michael Zhang (MediSync InfoSec), Laura Kim (CTO), Raj Patel (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Discussed SOC2/ISO status, KMS/customer-managed keys, data residency, whether prompts/content are retained or used for training, PHI handling and BAA options, next steps to share certs and technical docs.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Sam from Redwood, AE. With me are Priya, our SE, and Elena from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Michael Zhang: Good, thanks. I'm Michael, head of InfoSec at MediSync. We've got Laura and Raj on as well. Appreciate the time.
[00:13] Sam Carter: Great. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO, SSO/RBAC, audit logs & retention, KMS and encryption, and the big one — data handling: prompt retention, PII/PHI, and training on customer data. Priya will handle the technical bits.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Hi all. I'll jump in on the architecture side as we go.
[00:28] Laura Kim: We operate in healthcare so PHI is a big deal. We need clarity on whether Redwood ever uses customer prompts to train models and how long prompts are retained.
[00:36] Sam Carter: Absolutely. Quick top-level: for our hosted offering, default retention for request/response payloads is X days, but for enterprise we offer options — dedicated and private deployment where you control retention and keys. Also we have a contractual no-training clause — we don't use customer data to train our public models.
[00:52] Raj Patel: Can you say that on record? Written confirmation?
[00:55] Sam Carter: Yes, we can provide contract language and a security addendum. We'll share the standard clause.
[01:00] Michael Zhang: When you say "don't use customer data to train models" — does that include telemetry, aggregated logs, or only training corpora?
[01:08] Priya Nair: Good question. Internally, we separate telemetry from training data. By default we do not ingest customer request/response payloads into model training. We do use aggregated service metrics for platform improvement, but not raw prompts. For customers who need it, we offer a private deployment or dedicated capacity where you get full isolation and we don't have access to the payloads.
[01:26] Michael Zhang: Okay. How is that enforced technically? Any side channels?
[01:29] Priya Nair: Enforcement is both architectural and policy. Architecturally: request data for hosted tenants is stored in an encrypted S3-like store with access controls; automated pipelines that feed training corpora are separate and require explicit approvals; logs used for platform metrics are scrubbed and aggregated. For dedicated/private, the control plane can be customer-controlled and we can integrate with your KMS so keys are customer-managed.
[01:47] Sam Carter: To add — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certifications; Priya will explain how audit logs and RBAC are exposed for customers.
[01:54] Priya Nair: Sure. On RBAC and SSO: we support SAML 2.0 with Okta, Azure AD. Role mapping supports fine-grained roles: admin, deployer, observer, etc. All actions that change config or access secrets are audited.
[02:10] Laura Kim: We need proof that admin actions are logged — ideally immutable audit logs with export capability.
[02:15] Priya Nair: We provide an append-only audit log stream; customers can ship logs to their SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via secure syslog or cloud logging. Logs include user id, action, timestamp, IP, and request id. Retention is configurable but default is 90 days; for enterprise tiers we can extend or support customer-controlled retention in private deployments.
[02:34] Michael Zhang: What's the retention for request/response payloads by default in hosted? You said "X" earlier.
[02:39] Sam Carter: Sorry, default hosted retention is 30 days for request/response payloads and 90 days for audit logs/metadata. We can alter that for Dedicated or Private.
[02:48] Raj Patel: For HIPAA/PHI, we will likely require a BAA. Do you sign BAAs and is Redwood considered a business associate?
[02:55] Sam Carter: We do sign BAAs for customers using dedicated or private deployments; for hosted we evaluate case-by-case. Our legal team has a BAA template — we'll share.
[03:03] Laura Kim: Encryption specifics? At-rest and in-transit? Key management?
[03:07] Priya Nair: TLS 1.2+ in transit. At rest everything is AES-256. For hosted we encrypt with our KMS but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or bring-your-own-key for private deployments. We support envelope encryption for model cache and KV cache artifacts.
[03:23] Michael Zhang: Customer-managed keys — does Redwood have any access to plaintext when CMK is used?
[03:27] Priya Nair: If you provide CMK and restrict decryption to your account, Redwood processes can run in dedicated VPCs where encryption/decryption operations require those keys. In private on-prem installs, decryption never leaves your environment. For hosted with CMK, technical access paths require explicit provisioning; we can detail an architecture diagram showing how keys are used.
[03:47] Sam Carter: We'll include a network diagram in follow-up.
[03:49] Laura Kim: Auditability and attestations — do you publish SOC2 report and do you allow external auditors to review your controls?
[03:56] Sam Carter: Yes, SOC2 Type II is available under NDA; ISO27001 cert as well. External auditors can be coordinated through our security team. We'll send certs and the latest pen test summary.
[04:07] Michael Zhang: About training again — are there any circumstances where customer data could be used for model improvements? e.g., opt-in analytics or feedback programs?
[04:16] Priya Nair: Only with explicit customer opt-in. There's a separate data collection path for consented research/quality programs; that requires contractual approval and the data is isolated. Default is no.
[04:25] Raj Patel: On PII/PHI — do you have redaction tooling or DLP before storing prompts?
[04:30] Priya Nair: We offer optional pre-processing hooks. Customers can run client-side redaction or use our server-side plugins that can mask or hash fields before storage. For PHI-heavy customers we recommend using private deployments and on-prem redaction.
[04:44] Michael Zhang: If we use the hosted API but pass PHI accidentally, what's the incident response? Will Redwood notify? SLA for breach notification?
[04:52] Sam Carter: We have an incident response playbook and will notify customers per contract timelines; typical notification is within 72 hours for confirmed breaches. We'll include our incident response summary in the packet.
[05:03] Laura Kim: Data residency — we're primarily US/EU. Can you guarantee data stays in region?
[05:08] Priya Nair: Yes, we have region-specific deployments. For hosted tenants we can pin region so data resides in the US or EU. Dedicated and private give even stronger assurances.
[05:18] Michael Zhang: How does caching affect data residency — e.g., KV cache or prefix cache on GPU nodes? Could cache nodes be outside region?
[05:25] Priya Nair: Good callout. Cache nodes are co-located with serving in the chosen region. For multi-region failover we can configure routing policies; if you need strict residency we can disable cross-region fallback and ensure fail-closed behavior.
[05:40] Raj Patel: Are there export controls or lawful request processes we should be aware of?
[05:44] Sam Carter: We comply with lawful requests per applicable laws; we also publish our transparency report process. For enterprise customers, notification and legal cooperation are handled per contract and our legal team will coordinate.
[05:56] Michael Zhang: Back to logs: you said logs include IP. We need to ensure IP and user identifiers are stored in a way that supports forensic review but also can be redacted. Can we request a custom retention policy for PII fields?
[06:07] Priya Nair: Yes, we can support field-level redaction or pseudonymization. We'll include examples for Splunk export where you can choose fields to ingest.
[06:17] Laura Kim: On guarantees: we need a contractual clause that Redwood will not train models on our data and will not share PII/PHI with third parties except as necessary under contract or law.
[06:26] Sam Carter: We have standard non-training language and a data processing addendum that addresses sharing. We'll send those; subject to legal review but typically acceptable.
[06:34] Michael Zhang: For dedicated deployments, who manages the physical hardware — Redwood or customer? And can you provide a SOC style attestation for the dedicated environment?
[06:43] Priya Nair: For Redwood Dedicated, hardware is managed by Redwood in a cloud region, but the environment is single-tenant from the service perspective; we can provide additional attestations and we support network isolation and customer VPC peering. For ultimate control, our Private on-prem package places runtime in your environment and you manage hardware.
[07:00] Raj Patel: BAA again — do you have customers on BAA for similar healthcare workloads?
[07:05] Sam Carter: Yes, we have healthcare customers on BAAs with Dedicated/private deployments. We'll provide redacted references.
[07:11] Michael Zhang: Can you walk through an example incident: customer accidentally sends dataset with PHI to hosted API — what happens step by step?
[07:18] Priya Nair: Sure — detect via DLP or customer report, triage, isolate logs and payloads, rotate keys if needed, notify customer, run forensics in read-only mode, and remediate. For hosted we would quarantine affected storage and follow notification timelines. For private deployments much of that is in-customer control.
[07:38] Sam Carter: We should also discuss network controls — VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allow lists.
[07:43] Priya Nair: We support private endpoints and IP whitelisting. For dedicated customers, we can set up private networking with no public ingress.
[07:51] Laura Kim: On compliance evidence — can we get log samples that show audit events?
[07:56] Sam Carter: We'll produce redacted log samples and an event mapping doc for common actions.
[08:02] Michael Zhang: One more technical: is there any chance customer data is used to tune inference-serving caches or quantization heuristics that could leak info into model outputs for other tenants?
[08:13] Priya Nair: We have strict isolation in serving — cache warmup uses anonymized traces and we don't surface raw prompts across tenants. Quantization parameters are model-level and not per-tenant. For extra assurance, Dedicated/private has isolated cache and model instances.
[08:28] Raj Patel: Fine — that helps. What's the best way to get the legal/security docs?
[08:32] Sam Carter: We'll send a packet: SOC2, ISO cert, pen test summary, BAA template, DPA, and the KMS integration guide. We'll also include the redacted customer reference and architecture diagram.
[08:43] Elena Ruiz: I'll coordinate scheduling the follow-up VPC/baa deep dive with Priya and the legal team.
[08:48] Laura Kim: Sounds good. One last item: for monitoring — do you expose usage telemetry down to token level for cost accounting, and can that be redacted if containing PII?
[08:58] Priya Nair: We expose token-level billing and breakdowns; we can pseudonymize or redact payloads from those telemetry exports.
[09:08] Michael Zhang: Okay, that covers most questions. Would like to review the contract language before next meeting.
[09:13] Sam Carter: Understood. We'll send everything by Tuesday.
[09:17] Raj Patel: Thanks.
[09:18] Sam Carter: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts and schedule next deep-dive.

Meeting recap (auto): Redwood confirmed they do not use customer prompts for model training by default, offer private/dedicated options for stronger isolation and customer-managed keys, provide SOC2/ISO artifacts under NDA, support SAML/Okta and RBAC, have configurable retention for payloads and audit logs, offer field-level redaction and DLP hooks, and will share security packet and schedule follow-up VPC/BAA deep-dive.

Explicit next steps (recap): Sam to send certs and security docs; Priya to share KMS/Terraform integration and network diagrams; Elena to schedule follow-up; Michael to provide compliance checklist.

End of transcript.
